name: Adonijah
charge: Exalting himself to be king; asking for the king's concubine
summary: David's fourth son exalted himself, saying, I will be king, and gathered chariots, horsemen, Joab, and Abiathar for a coronation feast at En-rogel while David lay dying. Solomon was anointed the same day. Pardoned once, Adonijah then asked for Abishag the Shunammite.
offense: Adonijah exalted himself, saying that he would be king, and prepared chariots, horsemen, and fifty men to run before him. David had not displeased him by asking why he acted so (1 Kings 1:5-6). The display of succession grew without the father's correction, but display was not appointment. Joab and Abiathar supported him. He made a sacrificial feast and invited the king's sons and servants while leaving out Solomon, Nathan, Benaiah, and the mighty men (1 Kings 1:7-10). The invitations divided the house according to the claim he intended to establish. Religious sacrifice accompanied a decision made without the king's declaration. Nathan and Bathsheba brought the matter before David, who confirmed his oath that Solomon would reign. Solomon was placed upon the king's mule and anointed at Gihon by Zadok and Nathan (1 Kings 1:28-40). David also declared that the Lord had chosen Solomon to sit upon the throne (1 Chronicles 28:5). Adonijah's seniority among the surviving sons did not overrule that choice. When the news reached his feast, the guests rose in fear and departed. Adonijah caught hold of the horns of the altar and sought assurance that Solomon would not kill him (1 Kings 1:41-51). The man who had announced himself king now depended upon the king's mercy.
judgment: Solomon had spared him on condition of worthiness. The second offense was the end of it: Benaiah fell upon him and he died. Abiathar was banished and Joab executed in the same purge.

entries.commentary: David is old and cannot stay warm, so his servants seek a fair young woman to lie in his bosom and give him heat. This is one of the things that happens with age, when the body no longer produces heat as it did in youth and strength. Abishag the Shunammite is found and ministers to the king, but he does not know her. That means he did not have relations with her; she was there only to keep him warm. -
Adonijah exalts himself, saying he will be king, and prepares chariots and horsemen to promote himself. He takes the throne to himself rather than receiving it from the Most High.
David repeats the oath he swore by the Lord God of Israel, that Solomon his son shall reign after him and sit upon his throne in his stead. The throne belongs to Solomon by that sworn word. -

David commands that Solomon be set on the king's own mule and brought to Gihon, where Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him king over Israel. The people come up rejoicing so that the earth rings with the sound.

The days of David draw near that he should die, and he charges Solomon to be strong, to keep the charge of the Lord his God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his statutes, commandments, and judgments as written in the law of Moses, that he may prosper. There was a stipulation for the throne to continue: if his children take heed to their way and walk before the Most High in truth with all their heart, the throne stands. Reading through the kings, we see many who broke the commandments, and among their children some were righteous and some unrighteous. -
Solomon thrusts out Abiathar from being priest unto the Lord, fulfilling the word the Most High spoke concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh. The old judgment on Eli's line is carried out.

Joab, who had turned after Adonijah, flees to the tabernacle of the Lord and catches hold of the horns of the altar, but Solomon sends Benaiah to fall upon him. Joab dies for the innocent blood he shed when he slew Abner and Amasa, two men more righteous and better than he, without David's knowledge. The blood returns upon Joab's own head and upon his seed, while upon David and his seed and throne there shall be peace forever from the Lord. Benaiah is set over the host in his place.

Shimei is commanded to build a house in Jerusalem and dwell there, never crossing the brook Kidron on pain of death, and he agrees. After three years he goes to Gath after his runaway servants and breaks the oath, so Solomon has Benaiah put him to death, and the kingdom is established in Solomon's hand.

David said, This is the house of the Lord God, and this is the altar of the burnt offering for Israel. He commanded to gather together the strangers that were in the land of Israel and set masons to hew wrought stones to build the house of God. These strangers were brought in to help with the building of the temple. David prepared iron in abundance for the nails and for the joinings, brass in abundance without weight, and cedar trees in abundance. The Zidonians and they of Tyre brought much cedar wood to David.

David said that Solomon his son was young and tender, and the house to be built for the Lord must be exceeding magnifical, of fame and glory throughout all countries, so he prepared abundantly before his death. He called for Solomon his son and charged him to build a house for the Lord God of Israel.

David told Solomon that it was in his mind to build a house unto the name of the Lord, but the word of the Lord came to him saying he should not build it because he had shed blood abundantly and made great wars. Because of all the wars and fighting David had done, the Most High did not allow him to build the temple. The Lord promised David a son who would be a man of rest, to whom he would give rest from all his enemies round about, whose name would be Solomon, and in whose days he would give peace and quietness unto Israel. This son would build the house for the Most High's name, and the Most High would establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.

David charged Solomon that the Lord be with him and prosper him to build the house of the Lord his God, and asked that the Lord give him wisdom and understanding and charge concerning Israel that he might keep the law of the Lord. He said Solomon would prosper if he took heed to fulfill the statutes and judgments which the Lord charged Moses with concerning Israel. This is the same message the Most High gives us today: we will prosper as long as we obey the commandments. Be strong and of good courage; dread not, nor be dismayed.

In his trouble David prepared for the house of the Lord a hundred thousand talents of gold and a thousand thousand talents of silver, and brass and iron without weight, and timber and stone in abundance, telling Solomon he might add thereto. Without weight means they gave in such abundance they were not counting it. There were workmen with him in abundance, hewers and workers of stone and timber and all manner of cunning men for every kind of work. David told Solomon to arise and be doing, and the Lord be with him.

David commanded all the princes of Israel to help Solomon his son, asking whether the Lord their God was not with them and had not given them rest on every side, for he had given the inhabitants of the land into David's hand and the land was subdued before the Lord. This is what David was there to do: he subdued all the nations by the power of the Most High. He charged them to set their heart and soul to seek the Lord their God, to arise and build the sanctuary of the Lord God, and to bring the ark of the covenant and the holy vessels of God into the house that was to be built. Earlier David had moved the ark from place to place, and that is when he desired to build a house for it before the Lord.

*1 And David assembled all the princes of Israel, the princes of the tribes, and the captains of the companies that ministered to the king by course, and the captains over the thousands, and captains over the hundreds, and the stewards over all the substance and possession of the king, and of his sons, with the officers, and with the mighty men, and with all the valiant men, unto Jerusalem. 2 Then David the king stood up upon his feet, and said, Hear me, my brethren, and my people: As for me, I had in mine heart to build an house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and for the footstool of our God, and had made ready for the building: 3 But God said unto me, Thou shalt not build an house for my name, because thou hast been a man of war, and hast shed blood. 4 Howbeit the LORD God of Israel chose me before all the house of my father to be king over Israel for ever: for he hath chosen Judah to be the ruler; and of the house of Judah, the house of my father; and among the sons of my father he liked me to make me king over all Israel: 5 And of all my sons, (for the LORD hath given me many sons,) he hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel. 6 And he said unto me, Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father. 7 Moreover I will establish his kingdom for ever, if he be constant to do my commandments and my judgments, as at this day. 8 Now therefore in the sight of all Israel the congregation of the LORD, and in the audience of our God, keep and seek for all the commandments of the LORD your God: that ye may possess this good land, and leave it for an inheritance for your children after you for ever. 9 And thou, Solomon my son, know thou the God of thy father, and serve him with a perfect heart and with a willing mind: for the LORD searcheth all hearts, and understandeth all the imaginations of the thoughts: if thou seek him, he will be found of thee; but if thou forsake him, he will cast thee off for ever. 10 Take heed now; for the LORD hath chosen thee to build an house for the sanctuary: be strong, and do it. 11 Then David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch, and of the houses thereof, and of the treasuries thereof, and of the upper chambers thereof, and of the inner parlours thereof, and of the place of the mercy seat, 12 And the pattern of all that he had by the spirit, of the courts of the house of the LORD, and of all the chambers round about, of the treasuries of the house of God, and of the treasuries of the dedicated things: 13 Also for the courses of the priests and the Levites, and for all the work of the service of the house of the LORD, and for all the vessels of service in the house of the LORD. 14 He gave of gold by weight for things of gold, for all instruments of all manner of service; silver also for all instruments of silver by weight, for all instruments of every kind of service: 15 Even the weight for the candlesticks of gold, and for their lamps of gold, by weight for every candlestick, and for the lamps thereof: and for the candlesticks of silver by weight, both for the candlestick, and also for the lamps thereof, according to the use of every candlestick. 16 And by weight he gave gold for the tables of shewbread, for every table; and likewise silver for the tables of silver: 17 Also pure gold for the fleshhooks, and the bowls, and the cups: and for the golden basons he gave gold by weight for every bason; and likewise silver by weight for every bason of silver: 18 And for the altar of incense refined gold by weight; and gold for the pattern of the chariot of the cherubims, that spread out their wings, and covered the ark of the covenant of the LORD. 19 All this, said David, the LORD made me understand in writing by his hand upon me, even all the works of this pattern. 20 And David said to Solomon his son, Be strong and of good courage, and do it: fear not, nor be dismayed: for the LORD God, even my God, will be with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee, until thou hast finished all the work for the service of the house of the LORD. 21 And, behold, the courses of the priests and the Levites, even they shall be with thee for all the service of the house of God: and there shall be with thee for all manner of workmanship every willing skilful man, for any manner of service: also the princes and all the people will be wholly at thy commandment.*

When David was past the top of the hill, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him with saddled asses, two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred bunches of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a bottle of wine. When David asked where his master's son was, Ziba said Mephibosheth abode in Jerusalem, saying the house of Israel would restore him the kingdom of his father. So David gave Ziba all that pertained to Mephibosheth. Ziba came with gifts, and when David asked about Mephibosheth, Ziba claimed Mephibosheth thought the kingdom was about to be restored to him, which was not true. On that word David handed Ziba everything that belonged to Mephibosheth.

As David came to Bahurim, a man of the house of Saul named Shimei the son of Gera came out, cursing and casting stones at David and all his servants. Shimei cursed, calling David a bloody man and a man of Belial, saying the Most High had returned upon him all the blood of the house of Saul, and delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom his son, and taken him in his mischief because he was a bloody man. Shimei was of the house of Saul, and Saul was the wicked one who tried to kill David; it was by the hand of the Most High that Saul did not succeed. Yet Shimei cursed David as if David were in the wrong, because word gets around, people gossip and blame, and he saw David at a low state and went to rub it in his face. That is the mindset of some people in Israel as well.

Abishai the son of Zeruiah asked why this dead dog should curse the king, and offered to go take off his head. But the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? Let him curse, because the Most High hath said unto him, Curse David; who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so? David rolled with mighty men of war, so Abishai was ready to take Shimei's head off his shoulders. But David said to let him curse, for if it was of the Most High, then let him do it. Just as the Most High brings people to our forums and classrooms who bicker and try to bring confusion, it is of the Most High, sometimes to test the patience of those who pray for patience.

David said to Abishai and all his servants, Behold, my own son who came forth out of my bowels seeketh my life, how much more now may this Benjamite do it? Let him alone and let him curse, for the Most High hath bidden him. It may be that the Most High will look on his affliction and requite him good for the cursing this day. David reasoned that if his own son sought his life, this Benjamite was nothing; the Most High was doing this, so let him curse. It may be the Most High will look on all that was done to David and bless him in front of them, the same as when people try to bring us down and the Most High blesses us before them, which is why this congregation has grown exponentially.

David and his men went by the way while Shimei went along the hillside cursing, throwing stones, and casting dust; and they came weary and refreshed themselves. Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him. When Hushai the Archite, David's friend, came to Absalom saying, God save the king, Absalom asked why he went not with his friend, and Hushai answered that he would serve whom the Most High and Israel chose, and would serve in the presence of the son as he served the father. Hushai put into action the plan he and David made. Absalom challenged him, asking, Is this thy kindness to thy friend? Why wentest thou not with thy friend? This is a real friend, not a friendish one; a true friend tells you when you are wrong and full of it, not the one who only strokes your head and pats your back like Absalom did to steal the people's hearts.

Absalom asked Ahithophel for counsel, and Ahithophel said, Go in unto thy father's concubines whom he left to keep the house, and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father, and the hands of all with thee shall be strong. So they spread Absalom a tent on the top of the house, and Absalom went in unto his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel. The counsel of Ahithophel was as if a man had inquired at the oracle of God. Ahithophel counselled Absalom to lie with the ten concubines David left, in the sight of all Israel, on the roof of the house. This is the exact fulfillment of what the Most High spoke in chapter 12, that David's wives would be taken and one would lie with them in the sight of the sun, and that what David did secretly would be done before all Israel. It was not coincidence or irony; it was prophesied to happen, and none of it would have happened if David had not done what he did. The Most High keeps mercy and forgives, but by no means clears the guilty, so even when we come in and repent, we still must remember the fear of the Most High, for there is but one step between us and death.

verses.text: Then Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, I will be king: and he prepared him chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
And his father had not displeased him at any time in saying, Why hast thou done so? and he also was a very goodly man; and his mother bare him after Absalom.
And he conferred with Joab the son of Zeruiah, and with Abiathar the priest: and they following Adonijah helped him.
And Adonijah feared because of Solomon, and arose, and went, and caught hold on the horns of the altar.

And it was told Solomon, saying, Behold, Adonijah feareth king Solomon: for, lo, he hath caught hold on the horns of the altar, saying, Let king Solomon swear unto me to day that he will not slay his servant with the sword.
And Solomon said, If he will shew himself a worthy man, there shall not an hair of him fall to the earth: but if wickedness shall be found in him, he shall die.
So king Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar. And he came and bowed himself to king Solomon: and Solomon said unto him, Go to thine house.
And Adonijah the son of Haggith came to Bath–sheba the mother of Solomon. And she said, Comest thou peaceably? And he said, Peaceably.
He said moreover, I have somewhat to say unto thee. And she said, Say on.

And he said, Thou knowest that the kingdom was mine, and that all Israel set their faces on me, that I should reign: howbeit the kingdom is turned about, and is become my brother’s: for it was his from the Lord.
And now I ask one petition of thee, deny me not. And she said unto him, Say on.
And he said, Speak, I pray thee, unto Solomon the king, (for he will not say thee nay,) that he give me Abishag the Shunammite to wife.
And Bath–sheba said, Well; I will speak for thee unto the king.

Bath–sheba therefore went unto king Solomon, to speak unto him for Adonijah. And the king rose up to meet her, and bowed himself unto her, and sat down on his throne, and caused a seat to be set for the king’s mother; and she sat on his right hand.
Then she said, I desire one small petition of thee; I pray thee, say me not nay. And the king said unto her, Ask on, my mother: for I will not say thee nay.
And she said, Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah thy brother to wife.

And king Solomon answered and said unto his mother, And why dost thou ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? ask for him the kingdom also; for he is mine elder brother; even for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab the son of Zeruiah.
Then king Solomon sware by the Lord, saying, God do so to me, and more also, if Adonijah have not spoken this word against his own life.
Now therefore, as the Lord liveth, which hath established me, and set me on the throne of David my father, and who hath made me an house, as he promised, Adonijah shall be put to death this day.
And king Solomon sent by the hand of Benaiah the son of Jehoiada; and he fell upon him that he died.

Behold, a son shall be born to thee, who shall be a man of rest; and I will give him rest from all his enemies round about: for his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quietness unto Israel in his days.
He shall build an house for my name; and he shall be my son, and I will be his father; and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel for ever.
And of all my sons, (for the Lord hath given me many sons,) he hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.

And Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Go in unto thy father’s concubines, which he hath left to keep the house; and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father: then shall the hands of all that are with thee be strong.
So they spread Absalom a tent upon the top of the house; and Absalom went in unto his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.

lawsResolved.text: Rebellion and insurrection against the government is punishable by death.
Pride and arrogance brings decline, punishment and destruction.
Parents should sternly chastise and punish their children to put them on a righteous course - For he who spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves his son disciplines him diligently.
Primary part of inheritance to go to firstborn son rather than a favored son.
The powers of government are appointed by God and are in His hand.
